pages.text: On white-hot platinum, ammonia burns to nitric oxide: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O. Too cool, or too long on the gauze, and it burns to plain nitrogen instead. The $(item)Ostwald Converter$() sets the gauze temperature and the contact time: hot (about 1100-1200 K) and brief (a millisecond or two) for 90% selectivity. The nitric oxide is absorbed into $(fluid)Nitric Acid$().
The $(item)Platinum-Rhodium Gauze$() loses platinum above 1250 K. Iron meteorites carry the platinum metals: dissolve the iron away in sulfuric acid and they are left behind.
